title: Days of Notice Given on a Lease Term Agreement Exit Request — Weekend Counting
content:
**Rule.** For an insufficient notice charge on a lease-break request against a Lease Term Agreement, the days of notice given are counted in one of three ways: a request received on a Saturday or Sunday is counted from the following Monday, the next business day, to the termination date; a request received on a weekday for a termination date that falls on a Saturday or Sunday is counted from the received date to the Friday before the termination date; any other request is counted in calendar days from the received date to the termination date.

**Q. What is the received date?** The date the lease-break request was submitted.

**Q. How is "from one date to another" counted?** As the number of calendar days by which the first date precedes the second.

**Q. Which way applies when a weekend request also names a weekend termination date?** The first: a request received on a Saturday or Sunday is always counted from the following Monday to the termination date itself.

| Received on | Termination date falls on | Counted |
|---|---|---|
| Saturday or Sunday | any day | from the following Monday to the termination date |
| Monday to Friday | Saturday or Sunday | from the received date to the Friday before the termination date |
| Monday to Friday | Monday to Friday | from the received date to the termination date |

**Q. Worked cases? (hypothetical)**

- Received on a Saturday, termination date a Wednesday 39 calendar days later: counted from the Monday two days later, 37 days.
- Received on a Sunday, termination date a Friday 40 calendar days later: counted from the Monday one day later, 39 days.
- Received on a Tuesday, termination date a Sunday 47 calendar days later: counted to the Friday two days before it, 45 days.
- Received on a Tuesday, termination date a Saturday 46 calendar days later: counted to the Friday one day before it, 45 days.
- Received on a Monday, termination date a Thursday 45 calendar days later: 45 days.
